title: Claimant Identity Verification Deadline, Extensions, Expiry and Late Reopening
content:
Every Claimant Identity Verification case runs against a verification deadline, which may be extended on request and, once the case has expired, may give way to a late reopening with good cause.

## 1. Notice and deadline

The verification notice is sent through the pathway's notice channel on the day the case is opened, and the verification deadline is the notice date plus the pathway's deadline days, counted in calendar days.

## 2. Extensions

2.1 A deadline extension may be granted only when it is requested on or before the verification deadline.

2.2 The extension limit is counted in calendar days, and a request made on the deadline date itself is in time. The grace allowed for an extension request after the deadline date is 0 days: a request made on any day after the deadline date is not in time.

2.3 The test is made against the verification deadline recorded on the case, before the extension is granted.

2.4 Each extension adds the pathway's extension days to the current deadline, and no more extensions are granted than the pathway's maximum. The extensions still available on a case are the pathway's maximum less the extensions already granted on it, and never fewer than zero.

## 3. Expiry

3.1 A case not verified by the end of its deadline date expires.

3.2 On mail pathways whose timeliness basis is the postmark, documents postmarked on or before the deadline are reviewed even when they arrive later, and the case is not expired while that review runs.

## 4. Late reopening with good cause

4.1 An expired case may be reopened with good cause only on or before the late completion window after the verification deadline.

4.2 The late window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the verification deadline, and a request on the last day is in time. The test is made against the verification deadline recorded on the case, before the case is reopened.

4.3 A reopened case receives a new deadline of the pathway's extension days from the reopening date; a case not reopened in time stays expired and the linked claim stays on hold.

## 5. Pathway changes

Changing pathway never restarts the deadline.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical pathway with 21 deadline days, 14 extension days, one extension allowed and a 30-day late window)

| Hypothetical fact | Judgement |
|---|---|
| Case opened and notice sent on 1 March | Deadline is 22 March (1 March plus 21 calendar days) |
| Extension requested on 22 March | In time: the request falls on the deadline date itself |
| Extension requested on 23 March | Not in time: the request falls after the deadline date |
| Extension granted on a request made 20 March | New deadline is 5 April (22 March plus 14 days); no further extension remains |
| Case not extended and not verified by the end of 22 March | Case expires |
| Late window | Day 1 is 23 March; day 30 is 21 April |
| Reopening requested with good cause on 21 April | In time: last day of the window |
| Reopening requested on 22 April | Not in time: the case stays expired and the linked claim stays on hold |
| Case reopened on 10 April | New deadline is 24 April (10 April plus 14 days) |
